title: quercus pedunculata subsp. appenina
intro: Quercus pedunculata subsp. appenina, commonly known as a subspecies of the pedunculate oak tree, is a deciduous tree native to the Italian Alps. The health benefits of Quercus pedunculata subsp. appenina include its ability to act as an antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial agent, which can help to protect against cell damage, reduce inflammation, and prevent infections. The therapeutic actions of this plant include its use in traditional medicine to treat various conditions such as fever, rheumatism, and gastrointestinal issues. The bioactive constituents of Quercus pedunculata subsp. appenina include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
